Delhi Implements Fixed-Term Winter Pollution Curbs Starting November 1

02 Nov 2026, 08:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.thehindu.com

Overview of Winter Restrictions

The Delhi government is set to enforce a series of fixed-term winter pollution control measures starting November 1. These regulations are designed to curb air pollution during the peak winter window and operate independently of daily Air Quality Index (AQI) fluctuations, differing from the short-term emergency measures typically managed under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

Key Restrictions and Measures

  • Construction Ban: A total ban on dust-generating demolition and outdoor construction activities will be in place from November 1 to January 31. Essential public infrastructure projects, along with internal tasks such as plumbing and electrical work, are exempt provided they comply with dust control norms.
  • Vehicle Restrictions: Non-Delhi-registered vehicles below BS-VI emission norms face entry restrictions into the city. Electric, CNG, emergency, and sovereign duty vehicles are exempt.
  • Work From Home Mandate: Government and private offices are required to implement a mandatory 50% work-from-home arrangement. Essential and emergency services are exempt.
  • Parking Fee Hikes: Authorized parking fees will be doubled from November 1 through February 28, though parking charges at Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) facilities will remain unchanged.
  • Office Timings: To stagger traffic congestion, Delhi government offices will operate from 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., while Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) offices will function from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. until February 28.
  • Fuel Station Enforcement: Vehicles lacking a valid Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) will be denied fuel at fuel stations year-round.

Implementation and Verification

Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa reported that enforcement authorities plan to exercise some flexibility, requesting voluntary compliance rather than causing immediate inconvenience to the public up to Deepavali. Border monitoring will target non-compliant vehicles entering from neighboring states. Special enforcement teams, Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras, and AI-enabled command centers will assist in monitoring adherence.

Citizens can verify official updates and specific guidelines by reviewing notifications issued directly by the Delhi government's Department of Environment or consulting official announcements reported by accredited news organizations.
